boundary: The production notification-open journey (real FCM delivery, real OS tap, warm/cold/same-peer) as a separately named tap latency measurement: interval (a) Dart open receipt to first readable frame, interval (b) device clock before the tap to that event
limitations: Interval (a) is production's own NOTIFICATION_TAP_TO_MESSAGE_TIMING; for the cold tap it excludes process start. Interval (b) is an upper bound including the shade swipe and Maestro start-up. The original benchmark sets its tap time on fake services, so the numbers are not comparable. No latency threshold, as in the original.
ui_driver_reason: Maestro drives all ordinary UI and native notification taps. Narrow production observers establish exact route counts, already-active guard, unread state and database row identity; verified owned-UID process death preserves the native card for cold-tap startup, which force-stop cannot establish. Existing state guard verifies restoration.
discovery_reason: manifest-owned production notification tap latency (notification-open journey with --measure-tap-latency); original benchmark retained
reason: Additive production tap latency measurement on the notification-open journey; the original benchmark and the notification-open capability remain intact.
